text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Police officials arrested a group of 69 Asian illegal immigrants Tuesday night. It was the sixth and the biggest group of immigrants detained in Marijampole region this year so far.

- Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Stankevicius made confidential suggestions to Latvian counterpart Andris Shkele on their border dispute in a telephone conversation. It is expected that a meeting in the next week or two could lead Latvian and Lithuanian negotiations over their sea border out of deadlock.

- A 40-year-old journalist and artist, the father of six children and the head of Catholic radio 'Little studio', Vaidotas Zukas, who advocates 'tough democracy' declared his intention to be a candidate in 1998 presidential elections.
- Mazheikiu Nafta with the help of French Elf company intends to start production of jet fuel A1 this year.
- The Bank of Lithuania report shows that the assets of the bank were at 3.9 billion litas at the end of August, the highest since December 1992. 87 percent of it were foreign assets.
- The Bank of Lithuania reports that there were 2.9 billion litas in circulation in Lithuania at the end of August.

- Russian gas concern Gazprom resumed direct gas supply to Lithuania on October 1 and Lietuvo Dujos receives now 5.5 million cubic meters of gas per day. Lithuania owes Gazprom 65 million litas, 33.2 million litas to intermediary Stella Vitae and 24.2 million litas to Viconda.
- An IMF report forecasts 1.6 percent economic growth, 25 percent inflation and 3.4 percent fiscal deficit this year.
- Prosecutor's Office passed the case of suspected leader of Kaunas criminal world Henrikas Daktaras to court on Wednesday.

- Baltic countries which are not likely to get into the first round of NATO expansion are taking more active diplomatic steps to get at least into the second stage but the answer they get is that 'the doors remain open'. Lithuanian Foreign Minister Povilas Gylys leaves for the U.S. next week to discuss the plans for NATO expansion and Lithuania's chances.

- Nearly all Lithuanian political parties are unanimous over the main direction of foreign policy but the climate of Lithuanian international politics could become worse if the opposition, which tends to evaluate negatively neighbouring countries, wins the October parliament elections, Gylys said.

- Gylys also said that the resolution of the U.S. House of Representatives to encourage Russia to demilitarise the Kaliningrad region and to involve the territory into cooperation programs with the Baltic countries fully corresponds to Lithuania's position over this Russian enclave.
